aboutHistoryText1: KSC Wiedikon was founded in 1982 by three physical education teachers — Václav Arazim, René Zeender and Sylvia Schaerer. From the very first season, both basketball and volleyball players took to the court as KSCW members. What began as a neighbourhood initiative of enthusiastic athletes quickly grew into a staple of Zurich's recreational sports scene. Thanks to committed members and strong youth development, the club was able to steadily build new teams from its earliest years.
aboutHistoryText2: In the years that followed, KSC Wiedikon broadened its offering: badminton was played for several seasons from 1985, and floorball (Unihockey) for a time from 1989. On the competitive side, the women’s basketball team was one of the club’s flagships, battling for points in National League B for several years. Today KSC Wiedikon is one of the largest multi-sport clubs in Zurich’s District 3, with teams ranging from regional leagues to recreational sport. The close ties to the Wiedikon neighbourhood, the family-like atmosphere and the passion for sport remain the foundation of the club.
aboutCommunityText: At KSC Wiedikon, togetherness is at the heart of everything we do. Whether on or off the court — we are one team. New members are warmly welcomed and quickly find their place in our diverse club family.
aboutFairplayText: Respect towards opponents, referees, and teammates is a given for us. We always compete fairly — in training, in matches, and in club life.
aboutDevelopmentText: From the first trial training to the regional league, we foster the athletic and personal development of our members. Our coaches rely on modern methods and individual support.

membershipRegistrationText: Becoming a KSCW member is simple. Just three easy steps:
membershipStep1Text: Come to a training session with no obligation and get to know the team. You can attend up to three trial sessions before deciding. Simply sign up via the contact form or email.
membershipStep2Text: After your trial session you sign up using the online form. You will need your personal details, payment details and — for teams that require a licence — an identity document and a passport photo. Confirmation arrives by email.
membershipStep3Text: You'll receive a confirmation email with all further information — access to the members' platform, training times, and contact persons for your team.
schedulingIntroText1: KSC Wiedikon's game scheduling enables efficient coordination of home games. On game Saturdays, home games are grouped so that multiple teams can play on the same day in different time slots. The scheduling automatically considers hall availability, referee assignments, and conflicts.
schedulingIntroText2: Opposing teams can book their preferred game dates directly through our online tool. Confirmation is sent automatically via email.
schedulingSaturdaysText: On game Saturdays we group home games across our halls. Three time slots are available per Saturday, so several teams can play simultaneously or consecutively.
schedulingOpponentsText: As an opposing team, you can book your home game dates with us directly online. You'll receive a personalised link to the scheduling tool from your KSCW contact. There you can see all available dates and time slots and select your preferred date.

privacySubtitle: Information about how we handle your data
privacyIntro: KSC Wiedikon takes the protection of your personal data seriously. We treat your personal data confidentially and in accordance with Swiss data protection legislation (DSG) and this privacy policy.
privacyResponsibleText: Responsible for data processing on this website is:
privacyCollection: Collection and storage of personal data
privacyHostingText: Our website is hosted and delivered by Cloudflare, Inc. (101 Townsend St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). When you open a page, Cloudflare processes technical connection data — including your IP address, the time of the request, the URL requested, and browser and operating-system details — in order to deliver the page and defend against attacks. This may involve transferring data to the USA. A data-processing agreement is in place with Cloudflare: their Data Processing Addendum forms an integral part of the subscription terms we accepted. The club database runs on a server operated by Hetzner Online GmbH in the Nuremberg data centre (Germany); a data-processing agreement is in place with Hetzner too. Processing is based on our legitimate interest in providing the website securely and efficiently.
privacyCollectionText: When you visit our website, technical information is recorded automatically in server log files. This covers browser type, operating system, referrer URL, IP address and the time of the request. An IP address counts as personal data. We do not analyse these records statistically, build no usage profiles from them and do not combine them with other sources; they serve solely to operate the website securely and reliably.
privacyContactText: When you send us enquiries via the contact form or feedback form, your details (name, email address, message) are stored for processing the enquiry. Contact form data is deleted after the enquiry is resolved, at the latest after 90 days. Feedback data is retained until the suggestion is implemented or declined. We will not share this data without your consent.
privacyCookiesText: This website sets no cookies at all — none of our own, none from third parties, and in particular no tracking or marketing cookies. No web analytics of any kind is in use. Your browser’s local storage holds just three display preferences that you chose yourself: colour scheme (light or dark), language, and the roster view you last selected. None of this ever leaves your device or identifies you. Because no consent-requiring technology is used, this website needs no cookie banner.
privacyErrorTrackingText: We use Sentry to detect and fix technical faults (Functional Software, Inc.; data stored on servers in Germany). The Sentry script loads on every page view, but data is only transmitted when an error actually occurs — at which point it sends technical details such as browser type, operating system, the error itself and the page you were on. It captures no names, email addresses or form input. Processing is based on our legitimate interest in the stability and security of the website.
privacyThirdPartyText: Our website uses OpenStreetMap for map views. When loading the map, data is transmitted to the OpenStreetMap Foundation. For more information, please refer to OpenStreetMap's privacy policy. On team pages, Instagram content may be embedded. This content is only loaded after your explicit consent. When loaded, data is transmitted to Meta Platforms Ireland Ltd.
privacyRightsText: You have the right to information, correction, and deletion of your personal data stored by us. For corresponding enquiries, please contact:
privacyChangesText: We reserve the right to amend this privacy policy from time to time to ensure it always complies with current legal requirements. The current privacy policy applies to each subsequent visit.

bbScorerSubtitle: Training and materials for table officials (OTR1/OTR2)
bbScorerIntro: Table officials run the scoresheet, the game clock and the shot clock — no game happens without them. Training and licensing go through ProBasket, the north-eastern Swiss basketball association. Here you'll find the path to an OTR licence and all the materials at a glance.
bbScorerOtr1Desc: Qualifies you to work as scorer and timekeeper. This is the entry point for every new table official.
bbScorerOtr2Desc: Additionally qualifies you to operate the shot clock (24 seconds). Which league requires which level is set out in ProBasket's Weisungen Sport.
bbScorerPathTitle: How to get your OTR licence
bbScorerStep1Desc: ProBasket runs the training on OpenOlat. The guides for registration and login are in the materials below.
bbScorerStep2Desc: The platform's catalogue has exercises on the scoresheet, game clock and shot clock. The training modules below cover the same ground.
bbScorerStep3Desc: The exam is online and can be retaken as often as you like. You have to sit it yourself.
bbScorerStep4Desc: Once you pass, your OTR licence is entered in Basketplan within three working days. So sit the exam in good time before your first assignment.
bbScorerRefresher: Refresher: every two years ProBasket runs an online refresher exam. Fail it and your OTR licence lapses.
bbScorerRevocation: Losing the licence: if a referee files two reports of insufficient performance in the administrative report, the OTR licence is withdrawn.
bbScorerResourcesIntro: Every document comes straight from ProBasket's cloud, so it is always the current version.
bbScorerProBasket: For everything else about the officials system — regulations, FAQ and contacts — head to ProBasket.

privacySecurityText: Our public forms — contact, feedback, club registration, newsletter, and tournament and course sign-ups — are protected against automated submissions by Cloudflare Turnstile. Turnstile checks in the background whether input comes from a human, processing technical details about your browser along with your IP address. It sets no cookies and is not used for advertising. The provider is Cloudflare, Inc., USA.
privacyNewsletterText: For the newsletter we store your email address. Sign-up uses double opt-in: you first receive a confirmation email and are only added once you confirm. Every newsletter contains an unsubscribe link, and your address is deleted from the list once you unsubscribe.
privacyRegistrationText: If you apply for membership through the registration form, you provide the details needed for membership, invoicing and playing eligibility — including name, address, date of birth, contact details, AHV number and payment details, plus an identity document and passport photo for teams that require a licence. We pass this on only to the relevant federations and only as far as a playing licence requires: Swiss Volley and the regional association SVRZ, or Swiss Basketball and ProBasket. We process it for the duration of your membership and delete it afterwards unless statutory retention obligations apply — in particular the ten-year retention period for business records under Art. 958f of the Swiss Code of Obligations. For minors, registration is completed by a parent or guardian.

faqSubtitle: What to know before your first session
faqIntro: These are the questions we get asked most. Missing yours? Write to us and we’ll add it.
faqTrialQ: Can I try a session before joining?
faqTrialA: Yes. You can attend up to three trial sessions before deciding. Send us a quick message through the contact form first, so the team knows you’re coming and you turn up in the right hall.
faqSignupA: After your trial session, through the online registration form. You’ll need your personal details, payment details and — for teams that play with a licence — an identity document and a passport photo. Confirmation arrives by email.
faqCostA: The fee depends on the sport and category and covers a full season, September to June. Current amounts are on the membership page. The federation licence is not included in the fee but is billed on the same invoice.
faqGuestQ: Can I train as a guest?
faqGuestA: Yes. Guests train with a team and pay CHF 110 less than the regular membership fee, and the surcharge for not holding a scorer licence does not apply to them. Sign up through the same form, choosing the “Guest” role.
faqScorerQ: What is the scorer / officials duty?
faqScorerA: Active members take on scorer or table-official duties during the season. If the duty is not fulfilled, the membership fee increases by CHF 100. The club runs the required courses itself, separately for volleyball and basketball.
faqTrainingTimesQ: When and where does my team train?
faqTrainingTimesA: Weekday, time and venue are on every team page under “Training”. KSC Wiedikon trains in several halls in and around Zürich-Wiedikon; the exact hall and its address are listed with each team.
faqVolleyKidsA: At KSC Wiedikon, volleyball starts at U20. Younger children play basketball with us, where there are teams from U8 through U18.
faqBasketAgeQ: From what age can my child play basketball?
faqBasketAgeA: From U8. The junior programme runs from U8 and U10 (mixed) through U12 and U14 up to U16 and U18. Which birth years belong to which team is stated on the juniors page, and updates itself every season.
faqMoreA: Write to us through the contact form. You’ll also find the right person to talk to there for juniors, sponsoring or a specific team.
